Judgment

1. This is a revision petition under Section 397 of Cr.P.C. filed against order dated 12.04.2018 passed by Ld Trial court whereby charge for offence punishable U/s 498A IPC was framed against accused Salman and all the remaining accused persons were discharged for offences punishable U/s 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC.

2. The facts in brief of the revision are that the revisionist filed a complaint in PS Sangam Vihar against her husband, mother in-law, father -in-law, sister-in-laws, and brother in laws for demanding dowry as well as harassing, torturing her mentally and physically.

As per the averments the marriage between the revisionist and accused Salman got solemnized on 01.01.2012 at Delhi and immediately after marriage, the respondents started torturing her saying that she is not beautiful,
she is uneducated and that she has not brought any dowry.
It was alleged that her husband and respondents asked her to bring Rs.2 Lac and also beat her.

On 29.04.2013, her sister in law Shabana bit her on the shoulder and her other sister in laws pulled her from hair and her mother in law slapped her, after which she got herself treated from Safdarjung Hospital.

They kept on asking her to bring Rs. 2 Lac and again on 12.05.2013 they beat her, the complaint of which Cr. Rev 151/2019 by Praveen Khatoon Vs. Abdul Salam and Ors PURSHOTTAM PURSHOTTAM PATHAK PATHAK Date: 2024.02.16 16:31:37 +0530 she filed on the same day at Police Station.

sentences.text: In the month of September 2013, accused persons threw her from the house and are even not returning clothes, cash and jewelleries, which are in their custody.
It was alleged that they also threatened her.
3. On these allegations, instant FIR under section 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC was registered against the husband, mother in law and the respondents and the matter was investigated.
4. Ld.

Trial Court vide impugned order found sufficient material to frame charge against the accused Salman and discharged Abdul Salam, Salim, Ateeq, Nazim and Sabana, for offences u/s 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC, and Salman for offence u/s 406/323/506/34 IPC.

5. Being aggrieved by the order of framing of charge vide order dated 12.04.2018, revisionist has preferred this revision petition on following grounds:-
i. Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate the facts of the case and discharged all the respondents from the offences u/s 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC.
ii. Ld. Trial Court did not consider the fact that all the respondents committed offences against the revisionist/ complainant.
iii. The order of Ld. MM court is based on only presumptions, surmises, conjectures which are not relevant to the circumstances of the case.

6. Ld.
Counsel for revisionist argued on the line of grounds as taken in instant revision petition.

Ld.
Counsel vehemently argued that the Ld. Trial Court erred in law in passing the impugned order discharging the respondents.
It was argued that respondents intentionally harassed the revisionist with a demand of Dowry.
It was further argued that the alleged offences under section u/s 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC are made out against the respondents for which there is specific material on record.
On the strength of these arguments, revisionist pray for setting aside of the impugned order.

7. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for respondents argued that there is no infirmity in the impugned order as the same has been passed keeping in view the facts and material available on record and therefore the instant revision petition is liable to be dismissed.
8. I have heard rival contentions and perused the record.

9. Observations of trial court are reproduced as under:-
" Matter is pending consideration on point of charge.
The challan and all the accompanying documents have been perused.
Submissions have been heard.

On the basis of material on record, the court is of the view that there is a prima facie case made out against the accused Salman/ husband of the complainant as there are specific allegations attracting the ingredients of Sections 498A of IPC against the said accused.

General allegations have been Cr. Rev 151/2019 Digitally signed by Praveen Khatoon Vs. Abdul Salam and Ors PURSHOTTAM PURSHOTTAM PATHAK 2024.02.16 16:31:47 +0530 made against the remaining accused persons without specifying the role of the said accused persons.

Other than the said incident there is no other specific allegation against the remaining accused persons.
The remaining accused persons were put in column no. 12 of the charge sheet.
There is no MLC of the complainant of the year 2013.

It has been noted in a catena of judgments that whenever a matrimonial relation turns sour, there is a tendency to implicate the entire family of the husband.

10. Since the statutory provision of section 498A IPC has an important bearing in the present matter, therefore, same is being reproduced herein below for the sake of convenience :-
" Section 498A in The Indian Penal Code :-
498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.--Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall Cr. Rev 151/2019 by Praveen Khatoon Vs.

Explanation.--For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."
11.

If the allegations made by revisionist are tested upon the touchstone of aforesaid statutory principles, I am of the considered view that no charge under section 498A IPC is made out against respondents in the instant case.

In my opinion, even if all the allegations of the complainant are taken true on its face value, then also the case of complainant at best is that the respondents, since the date of marriage till the date she left the house, kept on asking from her to give Rs. 2 Lac.
There is nothing to substantiate that the said harassment was with a view to coercing her to bring the demanded money.

" 18.

14. Further, even if it is assumed that there was an entrustment, then also, I am of the considered view that only general and vague allegations have been made without elaborating upon the date,
time and place when the stridhan was handed over.
The details of said stridhan i.e. the number or the weight of jewellery articles, the amount of cash etc is also conspicuously missing in the instant case.
Further the revisionist herself has refused to take back these articles.

Therefore, in such an eventuality, it would be unsafe to hold that a grave suspicion arises against the said revisionists so as to charge them for offence under section 406 IPC.
15.

In my view, only vague and general allegations have been made by the complainant/revisionist in support of offences under section 498A/406 IPC and no specific role in furtherance of said general allegations have been attributed upon the respondents.
This simply leads to a situation where the specific role played by any of said respondents cannot be ascertained in the furtherance of the offence.
The allegations are general and omnibus and do not give rise to any grave suspicion against any of the said revisionists.

sentences.text: Though it can be argued that on the basis of the statement of complainant, a suspicion arises against the respondents, however it is a settled law that mere suspicion shall not suffice for framing charge against any accused and the test is that of 'grave suspicion'.

Reliance is placed upon judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal and Ors. ,
AIR 1979 SC 366, wherein it was held that the Court has the power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether a prima facie case against the accused is made out or not.

entities.text:
Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal and Ors. ,
AIR 1979 SC 366
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been further held that where the materials placed before the Court disclosed a grave suspicion against the accused, which has not been properly explained, the Court will be fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.

By and large, however, if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him gives rise to some suspicion, but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.
It is a settled law that the presumption howsoever strong cannot take the place of proof.

Relevant portion of the afore-mentioned judgment is reproduced hereunder:
"10.

Thus, on a consideration of the authorities mentioned above, the following principles emerge: (1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under Section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out:
(2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly Cr. Rev 151/2019 Digitally Praveen Khatoon Vs.

If the present case is tested upon the touchstone of settled principles of law, I am of the considered view that no grave suspicion arises against respondents, so as to charge them for offences U/s 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC.
21.
It may also be noted that order was passed on 12.04.2018 by Ld. MM and the present revision was filed on 09.04.2019.
The same was clearly beyond the limitation period.

The reason shown in condonation application is that the revisionist was not able to take appropriate steps due to non-awareness of the discharge of the respondents from the charges U/s 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC.
Perusal of Trial court record shows that revisionist was present on the date of order in court and even thereafter on each and every date.
The revisionist took almost a year to file the revision petition.

The said ground is not sufficient to condone the delay in filing the present petition as the Cr. Rev 151/2019 PURSHOTTAM PURSHOTTAM Praveen Khatoon Vs. Abdul Salam and Ors PATHAK Date: 2024.02.16 revisionist did not challenge the order despite having knowledge about it.
